content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I recently visited a client who has automated a motor with solar panels and an inverter. When I tried to connect using [product_name] [version_no], I couldn't connect at first due to subnet conflicts. After changing the IP address, I was able to connect and download the project, but attempting an online test resulted in a message indicating the projects didn't match—even though I retrieved the program directly from the device. I had to take the device away since the client didn’t need it immediately. I plan to run more tests and want to avoid this situation in the future. Can anyone advise what might have gone wrong?

If parameter values (like setpoints or times) are changed using the device's display, you'll see a warning from the software that the programs don't match when trying to go online. To resolve this, transfer the program from the device to your PC to create a new diagram, which will allow online monitoring.

After posting my question, I ran some tests by transferring the same program I downloaded from the device back to it, and this time I could perform the online test. It may have been exactly what you mentioned—the timers had started, causing a 'projects are not the same' issue. Apart from that, I’m not sure what else could have caused it, but it’s working now. Thanks for your quick reply.

I created a simple program for explanation and conducted an online test using the web server, so you can also observe value changes on the device's display. I also made a brief video showing this process.
I appreciate your thorough approach, [user_name]. You always go above and beyond.
Hello [user_name], glad I could help. Thanks for your feedback and rating.

analysis.insight_summary: Users experienced synchronization problems between the device and [product_name] when connecting via [product_name] [version_no]. Modifications made directly on the device's display led to a mismatch warning in the software, preventing online testing. Synchronizing the program by transferring it from the device back to the PC resolved the issue, highlighting the importance of keeping device and software configurations aligned.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect smooth online testing and automatic synchronization between [product_name] and the device, even when making parameter changes locally on the device display.
